key_insight: Training PV forecast models to predict multiple future time steps at once improves long-term temporal learning and accuracy across the forecast horizon.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable solar power predictions for grid operation with minimal added computational cost, supporting better integration of variable PV generation.
method: Combine ground-based sky images with historical PV output as inputs.
Train deep learning models with a multi-horizon objective instead of single-point forecasting.
Evaluate the approach across multiple architectures to test architecture-independent gains.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparative experiments across diverse deep learning architectures, showing stronger accuracy and robustness across multiple future horizons with negligible overhead.
watch_item: Performance gains may depend on the quality and temporal alignment of sky imagery and PV measurements, so deployment needs careful data synchronization and validation.
paper_title: Learning Long-Term Temporal Dependencies in Photovoltaic Power Output Prediction Through Multi-Horizon Forecasting
